title: Life outline; dam work and moving; returning to work
description: The interviewer asks Alice Ruth Pruitt to outline her life. She describes marrying a dam worker, traveling with construction jobs, and the difficulty of returning to daily work after time at home, including night shifts until 2 a.m.

title: Rural life versus city life; attitudes toward places
description: Pruitt compares rural dam towns with big cities, recalling a difficult month in Redding, California, and says she prefers rural Idaho. She argues that a positive attitude makes any place good.

title: Divorce; losing married friends; building new support
description: Pruitt describes the trauma of her divorce after six years, how married friends drifted away, and how she found new friends through work and the Shriners, with one particular friend helping her through.

title: Finding identity; putting oneself first; overcoming bitterness
description: She reflects on redefining herself after marriage, learning to set her own goals, shedding bitterness, and becoming comfortable with her new life and supportive friends.

title: Current work; childhood; dam camps and housing
description: Pruitt talks about her present job, and the conversation turns back to her childhood and the years following dam construction with her husband and young son, including living close to job sites.

title: Son's birth; medical care; recreation
description: She recalls her son's birth in the rural Ozarks with a clinic two miles away and wanting more children. She then lists her recreations: dancing, music, walking, and swimming with friends of both sexes.

title: Community attitudes; divorce stigma; travel
description: Pruitt says Lewiston people are generally friendly and she feels little stigma about being divorced. She describes group bus tours to Mexico and the Bahamas and meeting new people on those trips.

title: Garment factory work; further schooling; present happiness
description: She recalls fearing for her husband's health, taking a garment factory job while he was ill, and taking courses at a junior college in Redding. She says she is now happy and has rebuilt her life through church, friends, and work.

title: Marrying young; advice to young women; not being a doormat
description: Pruitt says she married at eighteen and would caution against marrying so young. She advises women to develop themselves, have goals, and not be doormats, arguing unhappiness is partly one's own responsibility.

title: Brothers; gender expectations; farm work before marriage
description: She talks about her two brothers and whether parents raise boys to be more competitive than girls. She recalls picking cotton and corn before marriage and preferring outdoor work to housework.

title: Changing times; openness; dancing and self-expression
description: Pruitt observes that society has opened up, with divorce and mixed social life now accepted. She describes dancing as self-expression and says living with someone before marriage is more accepted now.

title: Male-female friendship; closing reflections
description: She explains that she can now be friends with men without sex being assumed, something forbidden while she was married. The interview closes with appreciation for her openness and friendships across the states where she has lived.
